examInfo.title: CTFL - V4.0 - EN - SAMPLE EXAM - MODEL B

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a valid objective of testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To provide information for decision-making

options.label: b
options.text: To build confidence in the quality of the software

options.label: c
options.text: To guarantee that the software contains no defects

options.label: d
options.text: To detect failures and identify defects

a.explanation: Providing information for decision-making is a valid testing objective.

b.explanation: Building confidence in the quality of the software is a valid testing objective.

c.explanation: Testing cannot guarantee that software contains no defects. Testing can reduce the risk of defects remaining, but cannot prove their absence.

d.explanation: Detecting failures and identifying defects is a core testing objective.

questions.questionText: According to the 'defect clustering' principle, where are most software defects typically found?

options.label: a
options.text: Equally distributed across all modules

options.label: b
options.text: Only in recently added features

options.label: c
options.text: Concentrated in a small number of modules

options.label: d
options.text: Exclusively in integration points between components

a.explanation: Defects are not equally distributed; this is the opposite of what the defect clustering principle states.

b.explanation: While new features may have more defects, defect clustering is about concentration in specific modules, not just new code.

c.explanation: The defect clustering principle (also known as the Pareto principle in testing) states that a small number of modules contain the majority of defects.

d.explanation: Defects can cluster anywhere; the principle does not restrict clustering to integration points.

questions.questionText: Which of the seven testing principles states that testing all possible input combinations and preconditions is not feasible?

options.label: a
options.text: Testing shows presence of defects

options.label: b
options.text: Exhaustive testing is impossible

options.label: c
options.text: Defect clustering

options.label: d
options.text: Testing is context-dependent

a.explanation: This principle addresses what testing can prove, not feasibility of input coverage.

b.explanation: Exhaustive testing is impossible states that testing all combinations of inputs and preconditions is not feasible except in trivial cases; risk and priority are used to focus testing.

c.explanation: Defect clustering describes where defects tend to accumulate, not the infeasibility of exhaustive testing.

d.explanation: Testing is context-dependent means different contexts require different testing approaches.

questions.questionText: Which of the following activities belongs to the TEST ANALYSIS activity in the test process?

options.label: a
options.text: Scheduling test execution and assigning testers

options.label: b
options.text: Identifying test conditions from the test basis

options.label: c
options.text: Comparing actual vs expected results

options.label: d
options.text: Archiving test results for future reference

a.explanation: Scheduling and assigning testers is part of test planning.

b.explanation: Test analysis involves examining the test basis (requirements, designs, etc.) to identify what should be tested and derive test conditions.

c.explanation: Comparing actual vs expected results is part of test execution.

d.explanation: Archiving is part of test completion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is produced during the TEST DESIGN activity?

options.label: a
options.text: Test completion report

options.label: b
options.text: Defect reports

options.label: c
options.text: High-level test cases with expected results

options.label: d
options.text: Test environment setup records

a.explanation: The test completion report is produced during test completion.

b.explanation: Defect reports are produced during test execution when failures are detected.

c.explanation: Test design produces high-level test cases, test data requirements, and test environment requirements derived from test conditions.

d.explanation: Test environment setup records are produced during test implementation.

questions.questionText: A software component works correctly in isolation but fails when combined with another component. What type of defect is this?

options.label: a
options.text: A unit-level defect

options.label: b
options.text: An integration defect

options.label: c
options.text: A requirements defect

options.label: d
options.text: A performance defect

a.explanation: A unit-level defect would be found when testing the component in isolation, not in combination.

b.explanation: When components work individually but fail when combined, the defect is in the interface or interaction between them — an integration defect.

c.explanation: A requirements defect involves incorrect or missing requirements, not component interaction issues.

d.explanation: A performance defect relates to speed, resource usage, or scalability, not functional interaction issues.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an essential skill for testers according to ISTQB CTFL v4.0?

options.label: a
options.text: The ability to write source code in all programming languages

options.label: b
options.text: Analytical thinking and effective communication

options.label: c
options.text: Advanced mathematical knowledge

options.label: d
options.text: Prior work experience as a software developer

a.explanation: Testers do not need to write code in all languages; technical knowledge is helpful but not defined this way.

b.explanation: ISTQB lists analytical thinking, effective communication, curiosity, attention to detail, and domain knowledge as essential tester skills.

c.explanation: Advanced mathematics is not an essential skill for most testing roles.

d.explanation: Prior development experience is helpful but not identified as an essential skill for testers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes 'testing is context-dependent'?

options.label: a
options.text: The same test approach should be applied to all software projects

options.label: b
options.text: Testing for safety-critical systems requires different approaches than testing e-commerce websites

options.label: c
options.text: Testing must always follow the same sequence of activities

options.label: d
options.text: Context only matters during requirements analysis, not during testing

a.explanation: Using the same approach for all projects contradicts the context-dependent principle.

b.explanation: Testing is context-dependent means that different contexts require different approaches. Testing a safety-critical medical device requires very different rigor compared to testing an e-commerce website.

c.explanation: Test activities can vary in sequence and emphasis based on context.

d.explanation: Context matters throughout all testing activities, not just requirements analysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents 'whole team' approach to quality in Agile testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Only designated QA engineers are responsible for quality

options.label: b
options.text: All team members, including developers and business representatives, share responsibility for quality

options.label: c
options.text: Quality assurance is the responsibility of the project manager

options.label: d
options.text: Quality is verified only at the end of each release

a.explanation: The whole team approach explicitly rejects the idea that quality is only the QA team's responsibility.

b.explanation: The whole team approach in Agile means everyone on the team — developers, testers, business analysts, and others — shares responsibility for quality.

c.explanation: The project manager oversees the project but quality is a shared team responsibility.

d.explanation: Agile promotes continuous quality, not just end-of-release verification.

questions.questionText: In Agile development, which ceremony is used to plan and commit to work for the upcoming iteration?

options.label: a
options.text: Sprint retrospective

options.label: b
options.text: Daily standup

options.label: c
options.text: Sprint planning

options.label: d
options.text: Sprint review

a.explanation: The sprint retrospective is a meeting to reflect on the process and identify improvements.

b.explanation: The daily standup is a short daily meeting for synchronization, not planning.

c.explanation: Sprint planning is the ceremony where the team reviews the product backlog, selects items for the sprint, and commits to the work to be completed.

d.explanation: The sprint review demonstrates completed work to stakeholders, not plans for upcoming work.

questions.questionText: Which test level is PRIMARILY concerned with validating the system against user needs and business requirements?

options.label: a
options.text: Component testing

options.label: b
options.text: Component integration testing

options.label: c
options.text: System testing

options.label: d
options.text: Acceptance testing

a.explanation: Component testing validates individual units against their technical specifications, not user needs.

b.explanation: Component integration testing checks interfaces between components.

c.explanation: System testing validates the complete system behavior but does not specifically focus on user acceptance.

d.explanation: Acceptance testing validates whether the system satisfies user needs and business requirements, and determines if the system is ready for deployment.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of confirmation testing (re-testing)?

options.label: a
options.text: To check that the software performs well under load

options.label: b
options.text: To verify that a previously detected defect has been successfully fixed

options.label: c
options.text: To test newly added features in each release

options.label: d
options.text: To ensure no new defects were introduced by a change

a.explanation: Testing under load is performance testing.

b.explanation: Confirmation testing (also called re-testing) specifically verifies that the test case(s) that failed due to a defect now pass after the defect has been fixed.

c.explanation: Testing new features is part of the standard test cycle, not confirmation testing.

d.explanation: Ensuring no new defects were introduced is the purpose of regression testing.

questions.questionText: What is the PRIMARY objective of impact analysis in maintenance testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To create new test cases from scratch for the maintained system

options.label: b
options.text: To determine which parts of the system are affected by a change and what should be retested

options.label: c
options.text: To analyze the performance impact of adding new users to the system

options.label: d
options.text: To assess the financial cost of performing maintenance

a.explanation: While new tests may be written, the primary objective of impact analysis is to determine scope, not create tests.

b.explanation: Impact analysis in maintenance testing determines what areas of the system are affected by a change, which informs what needs to be regression tested.

c.explanation: User load analysis is a capacity planning concern, not impact analysis for maintenance testing.

d.explanation: Financial cost assessment is a project management activity, not the purpose of impact analysis.

questions.questionText: In Agile, which practice involves writing tests before writing the corresponding code?

options.label: a
options.text: Exploratory testing

options.label: b
options.text: Test-driven development (TDD)

options.label: c
options.text: Pair programming

options.label: d
options.text: Code review

a.explanation: Exploratory testing involves simultaneous test design and execution, not writing tests before code.

b.explanation: Test-driven development (TDD) requires writing an automated test before writing the production code that makes the test pass, then refactoring.

c.explanation: Pair programming involves two developers coding together, not writing tests first.

d.explanation: Code review examines existing code for quality, not a test-first practice.

questions.questionText: Which of the following work products CAN be examined using static testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Only source code files

options.label: b
options.text: Source code, requirements specifications, and design documents

options.label: c
options.text: Only compiled executable binaries

options.label: d
options.text: Only test execution logs

a.explanation: Static testing is not limited to source code; it applies to any work product.

b.explanation: Static testing can examine any work product including source code, requirements, designs, user stories, test cases, and other documentation.

c.explanation: Compiled binaries are examined through dynamic testing (execution), not typically through static analysis of the artifact itself.

d.explanation: Test execution logs result from dynamic testing; they are not the primary subject of static testing.

questions.questionText: Which type of review is led by the author of the work product?

options.label: a
options.text: Inspection

options.label: b
options.text: Technical review

options.label: c
options.text: Walkthrough

options.label: d
options.text: Informal review

a.explanation: Inspections are led by a trained moderator, not the author.

b.explanation: Technical reviews are peer-led by a trained moderator or technical lead, not the author.

c.explanation: Walkthroughs are led by the author, who guides the reviewers through the work product. The main purpose is learning and gaining feedback.

d.explanation: Informal reviews have no defined leader; they can be done by anyone.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a defect that is typically found by STATIC analysis tools but not by dynamic testing?

options.label: a
options.text: A performance bottleneck that occurs under high load

options.label: b
options.text: An unreachable code section

options.label: c
options.text: A user interface element that is misaligned

options.label: d
options.text: A timeout error in a network request

a.explanation: Performance bottlenecks are found by dynamic performance testing, not static analysis.

b.explanation: Static analysis tools can identify unreachable code (dead code) by examining code structure without execution. Dynamic testing cannot reach it by definition.

c.explanation: UI misalignment issues are found by visual/dynamic testing or UI review, not static code analysis.

d.explanation: Network timeout errors occur at runtime and are found through dynamic testing.

questions.questionText: What is the role of the moderator in a formal review?

options.label: a
options.text: To write the work product being reviewed

options.label: b
options.text: To facilitate the review process and ensure it runs effectively

options.label: c
options.text: To implement the changes identified during the review

options.label: d
options.text: To approve the final version of the work product

a.explanation: The author writes the work product; the moderator facilitates its review.

b.explanation: The moderator (facilitator) plans and leads the review meeting, ensures the process is followed, mediates discussion, and tracks actions.

c.explanation: The author is responsible for fixing defects found in the review.

d.explanation: Approval decisions may rest with management or the author, but not the moderator's primary role.

questions.questionText: A system displays different messages depending on a customer's age: under 18, 18-64, and 65+. Using equivalence partitioning, how many valid partitions exist?

a.explanation: There are multiple valid partitions corresponding to the age groups with different behavior.

b.explanation: There are 3 distinct valid ranges, not 2.

c.explanation: The three age groups (under 18, 18-64, 65+) each receive different outputs, making them 3 distinct valid equivalence partitions.

d.explanation: There are 3 valid partitions. Invalid partitions (e.g., negative ages) would be separate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sets of values represents a 3-value BVA test set for an integer field that accepts values from 1 to 10?

a.explanation: These 4 values represent 2-value BVA (boundaries plus just outside). 3-value BVA also includes values just inside the boundaries.

b.explanation: 3-value BVA tests the boundary, the value just inside, and the value just outside. For range 1-10: 0 (below), 1 (boundary), 2 (inside), 9 (inside), 10 (boundary), 11 (above).

c.explanation: This includes only the boundaries and a midpoint, not the systematic coverage required by 3-value BVA.

d.explanation: Only 2 values (boundaries only) is insufficient for either 2-value or 3-value BVA.

questions.questionText: When is decision table testing MOST appropriate?

options.label: a
options.text: When testing the system's behavior under different load conditions

options.label: b
options.text: When the system behavior depends on complex combinations of conditions

options.label: c
options.text: When testing a single numeric input range

options.label: d
options.text: When the tester wants to explore the system without predefined test cases

a.explanation: Load condition testing is performance testing, not a use case for decision tables.

b.explanation: Decision table testing is most effective when the system behavior varies based on combinations of multiple conditions, helping ensure all condition combinations are covered.

c.explanation: A single numeric range is best handled by equivalence partitioning and BVA.

d.explanation: Exploring without predefined test cases describes exploratory testing.

questions.questionText: A state transition diagram has 4 states and 6 transitions. What is the minimum number of test cases needed to cover all transitions?

a.explanation: 4 test cases would cover all states but not necessarily all transitions.

b.explanation: 5 test cases may not cover all 6 transitions.

c.explanation: To achieve 100% transition coverage, every transition must be executed at least once. With 6 transitions, 6 test cases are needed (one per transition, assuming optimal design).

d.explanation: 10 test cases would over-cover; only 6 are needed for all-transitions coverage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes branch coverage?

options.label: a
options.text: Ensuring every line of code has been executed

options.label: b
options.text: Ensuring both the true and false outcomes of every decision point have been executed

options.label: c
options.text: Ensuring every possible path through the program has been tested

options.label: d
options.text: Ensuring every method in the class hierarchy has been called

a.explanation: Ensuring every line is executed is statement coverage, not branch coverage.

b.explanation: Branch coverage (decision coverage) requires that both the true and false outcomes of every decision point in the code have been exercised.

c.explanation: Ensuring every possible path is path coverage, which is generally infeasible.

d.explanation: Calling every method is a type of method coverage, not branch coverage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes error guessing as a test technique?

options.label: a
options.text: Using automated tools to predict defect locations based on code metrics

options.label: b
options.text: Using the tester's knowledge and experience to anticipate likely defects and design tests for them

options.label: c
options.text: Randomly generating test inputs to discover unexpected failures

options.label: d
options.text: Reviewing test requirements to identify missing coverage areas

a.explanation: Error guessing is based on human experience and intuition, not automated code metrics.

b.explanation: Error guessing is an experience-based technique where testers use their knowledge of past defects, typical developer mistakes, and system complexity to anticipate where defects are likely to be found.

c.explanation: Randomly generating inputs describes random testing or fuzzing, not error guessing.

d.explanation: Reviewing requirements for coverage gaps is part of test analysis, not error guessing.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a test charter in exploratory testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To provide detailed step-by-step test procedures

options.label: b
options.text: To guide the scope and direction of an exploratory testing session

options.label: c
options.text: To record defects found during exploratory testing

options.label: d
options.text: To specify the test automation framework to be used

a.explanation: Detailed step-by-step procedures are scripted test cases, not exploratory test charters.

b.explanation: A test charter defines the mission of an exploratory testing session, including what to explore, the target, and the time box, while leaving latitude for the tester's judgment.

c.explanation: Defects are recorded in defect reports; the charter defines the session scope.

d.explanation: Automation framework selection is a technical infrastructure decision, not the purpose of a charter.

questions.questionText: Which collaborative test approach requires both the developer and tester to co-create tests from user stories before implementation?

options.label: a
options.text: Boundary value analysis

options.label: b
options.text: Acceptance test-driven development (ATDD)

options.label: c
options.text: White-box testing

options.label: d
options.text: Regression testing

a.explanation: BVA is a black-box test design technique, not a collaborative development practice.

b.explanation: ATDD involves the whole team (developers, testers, business stakeholders) in defining acceptance tests before implementation to clarify requirements and drive development.

c.explanation: White-box testing is a technique based on code structure, not a collaborative pre-implementation practice.

d.explanation: Regression testing validates that changes did not break existing functionality.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is typically included in a test plan according to ISTQB CTFL v4.0?

options.label: a
options.text: Individual test case steps and expected results

options.label: b
options.text: Risk register and testing approach

options.label: c
options.text: Detailed defect descriptions and resolution status

options.label: d
options.text: Source code listings for the modules under test

a.explanation: Individual test case steps belong in test specifications, not the test plan.

b.explanation: A test plan typically includes context, communication plan, risk register, testing approach, activities, estimates, schedule, and resources.

c.explanation: Defect descriptions and resolution belong in defect management records.

d.explanation: Source code is not part of a test plan.

questions.questionText: What is a project risk in the context of testing?

options.label: a
options.text: The risk that the software will fail to work correctly when deployed

options.label: b
options.text: The risk that a feature does not meet user expectations

options.label: c
options.text: The risk related to management, resources, or organizational factors that could affect the test project

options.label: d
options.text: The risk that security vulnerabilities will be found in production

a.explanation: Software failing when deployed is a product risk, not a project risk.

b.explanation: Features not meeting expectations is a product risk.

c.explanation: Project risks are risks related to the management of the test project, such as insufficient resources, unrealistic schedules, poor communication, or supplier issues.

d.explanation: Security vulnerabilities in production are product risks.

questions.questionText: A test manager estimates testing effort using data from similar past projects adjusted for project size. Which estimation technique is this?

options.label: a
options.text: Expert-based estimation

options.label: b
options.text: Ratio-based estimation (metric-based)

options.label: c
options.text: Planning poker

options.label: d
options.text: Wideband Delphi

a.explanation: Expert-based estimation is based on personal judgment, not data from past projects.

b.explanation: Metric-based (ratio-based) estimation uses historical data from previous similar projects and adjusts for the size and complexity of the current project.

c.explanation: Planning poker is a consensus-based expert estimation technique.

d.explanation: Wideband Delphi is an expert-based consensus technique, not metric-based.

questions.questionText: Which of the following test metrics reflects how well the testing has covered the specified requirements?

options.label: a
options.text: Defect density per module

options.label: b
options.text: Percentage of requirements covered by test cases

options.label: c
options.text: Number of testers on the team

options.label: d
options.text: Test execution time per test case

a.explanation: Defect density measures defects found, not requirements coverage.

b.explanation: Percentage of requirements covered by test cases is a coverage metric that shows how well the test suite addresses the specified requirements.

c.explanation: Team size is a resource metric, not a coverage metric.

d.explanation: Test execution time is an efficiency metric, not a coverage metric.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a purpose of test monitoring?

options.label: a
options.text: To create detailed test cases for each requirement

options.label: b
options.text: To collect information and compare actual progress against the test plan

options.label: c
options.text: To decide whether the system is ready for release

options.label: d
options.text: To identify test conditions from the test basis

a.explanation: Creating test cases is part of test design and implementation, not monitoring.

b.explanation: Test monitoring collects information about testing activities and compares actual progress against the plan to detect deviations and enable corrective actions.

c.explanation: Release decisions are typically made during test completion after evaluating exit criteria.

d.explanation: Identifying test conditions is part of test analysis.

questions.questionText: In the context of defect management, what does the term 'defect lifecycle' refer to?

options.label: a
options.text: The time it takes to fix a defect from discovery to closure

options.label: b
options.text: The sequence of states a defect goes through from detection to closure

options.label: c
options.text: The number of defects found per test cycle

options.label: d
options.text: The impact of a defect on the system's overall quality

a.explanation: The time to fix is a metric (resolution time), not the lifecycle itself.

b.explanation: The defect lifecycle describes the states a defect transitions through: from detection (New/Open), through assignment, analysis, fixing (Fixed/Resolved), verification (Re-test), to closure (Closed).

c.explanation: Number of defects per test cycle is a defect density metric, not the lifecycle.

d.explanation: Defect impact relates to severity, not the lifecycle definition.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about a test progress report is CORRECT?

options.label: a
options.text: It is produced only at the very end of the testing project

options.label: b
options.text: It provides regular updates to stakeholders on testing status and progress

options.label: c
options.text: It contains the complete list of all test cases to be executed

options.label: d
options.text: It replaces the test plan once testing begins

a.explanation: The test completion report is produced at the end; progress reports are produced regularly during testing.

b.explanation: Test progress reports are produced regularly (daily, weekly, per sprint) to communicate current testing status, metrics, and any deviations to stakeholders.

c.explanation: The complete list of test cases is in the test specification, not the progress report.

d.explanation: Progress reports supplement the test plan; they do not replace it.

questions.questionText: Why is it important to distinguish between the severity and priority of a defect?

options.label: a
options.text: Because a technically severe defect may have low business priority, or a minor defect may need urgent fixing

options.label: b
options.text: Because only high severity defects should be reported

options.label: c
options.text: Because severity is always more important than priority

options.label: d
options.text: Because defect priority determines which module the defect belongs to

a.explanation: A critical defect in a rarely-used feature may have low priority, while a cosmetic defect on the home page may have high priority due to business visibility. The distinction helps teams make correct repair decisions.

b.explanation: All defects should be reported regardless of severity; the team then decides priority.

c.explanation: Neither is inherently more important; they serve different decision-making purposes.

d.explanation: Priority does not indicate module location; that is tracked separately.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of 'test control' in the test management process?

options.label: a
options.text: To write automated test scripts

options.label: b
options.text: To take corrective actions when monitoring shows deviations from the test plan

options.label: c
options.text: To define the initial test objectives and scope

options.label: d
options.text: To prepare test data for test execution

a.explanation: Writing automated test scripts is part of test implementation, not test control.

b.explanation: Test control involves taking corrective actions based on information collected through monitoring, such as adjusting priorities, reallocating resources, or revising test plans.

c.explanation: Defining objectives and scope is part of test planning.

d.explanation: Preparing test data is part of test implementation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a test management tool?

options.label: a
options.text: A tool that automatically injects faults into code to test defect detection

options.label: b
options.text: A tool that tracks test cases, test runs, and defects in a centralized repository

options.label: c
options.text: A tool that measures CPU and memory usage during test execution

options.label: d
options.text: A tool that generates random input values for fuzz testing

a.explanation: A fault injection tool is used for robustness testing, not test management.

b.explanation: Test management tools maintain and track test cases, test plans, test execution status, and defects in a central repository accessible to the team.

c.explanation: CPU and memory measurement tools are performance monitoring tools.

d.explanation: Random input generators are test data tools or fuzzing tools, not test management tools.

questions.questionText: What is the MAIN reason that automated test maintenance effort is often underestimated?

options.label: a
options.text: Automated tests run faster than expected

options.label: b
options.text: The application and its tests must be updated whenever the software changes

options.label: c
options.text: Automated tests always find more defects than anticipated

options.label: d
options.text: Test managers do not understand automation tools

a.explanation: Test execution speed does not cause maintenance effort to be underestimated.

b.explanation: Automated tests require ongoing maintenance whenever the application changes. This ongoing cost is often underestimated, making automation appear cheaper than it is.

c.explanation: Finding more defects is a positive outcome, not a maintenance effort driver.

d.explanation: Manager understanding may vary, but the core reason for underestimation is the ongoing maintenance cost of keeping tests synchronized with the application.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of a good static analysis tool?

options.label: a
options.text: It executes the code to find runtime errors

options.label: b
options.text: It analyzes code without executing it to find potential defects and code quality issues

options.label: c
options.text: It generates test cases automatically based on the requirements

options.label: d
options.text: It simulates user interactions with the application

a.explanation: Executing code to find runtime errors is dynamic testing, not static analysis.

b.explanation: Static analysis tools examine code without executing it, identifying issues such as coding standard violations, unreachable code, undeclared variables, and security vulnerabilities.

c.explanation: Automatic test case generation from requirements is a different category of test tool.

d.explanation: Simulating user interactions is done by test execution tools, not static analysis tools.

questions.questionText: A tester achieves 100% branch coverage on a function. What can be said about statement coverage?

options.label: a
options.text: Statement coverage will be less than 100%

options.label: b
options.text: Statement coverage will also be 100%

options.label: c
options.text: Statement coverage and branch coverage are unrelated

options.label: d
options.text: Nothing can be said about statement coverage from branch coverage data

a.explanation: 100% branch coverage subsumes 100% statement coverage; statement coverage cannot be lower.

b.explanation: If 100% branch coverage is achieved, all branches (true and false) of every decision are executed, which means every statement is executed at least once, guaranteeing 100% statement coverage.

c.explanation: They are related: branch coverage subsumes (implies) statement coverage.

d.explanation: A clear relationship exists: 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage.

questions.questionText: In testing, what is a 'test basis'?

options.label: a
options.text: The minimum number of test cases required to cover all requirements

options.label: b
options.text: The body of knowledge used as the basis for test analysis and design

options.label: c
options.text: The set of all automated test scripts in the test suite

options.label: d
options.text: The test environment configuration used for test execution

a.explanation: The minimum number of test cases is a coverage goal, not the test basis definition.

b.explanation: The test basis is any document or other work product (requirements, design specs, user stories, source code) used as a reference for test analysis and design.

c.explanation: Automated test scripts are testware, part of the test suite, not the test basis.

d.explanation: Test environment configuration is infrastructure, not the test basis.
